review_scope: Paraphrased AWS source text. Layout suggestions are application-specific synthesis, not copied AWS diagrams or deployment certification.

patterns.title: Browser workbench and serverless API
patterns.use_when: A browser UI calls business APIs; evaluate static hosting when server rendering is unnecessary.
patterns.avoid: Do not assume every UI needs containers, a cache, or a load balancer.
patterns.flow: Browser -> CloudFront -> S3 UI assets; browser -> authenticated API Gateway -> Lambda business logic -> chosen data store.
patterns.layout: Separate UI asset delivery and API calls; place data beside its caller and identity beside ingress.
service_choices: S3/CloudFront serve static assets; API Gateway exposes APIs; Lambda implements custom logic.
Use the agreed identity provider; choose persistence by access patterns, not the reference's example application.
relationship_checks: Show the S3 origin connection when CloudFront serves an S3 UI.
Tokens authorize API calls; execution roles authorize service access. These are separate relationships.

patterns.title: Private application behind a load balancer
patterns.use_when: An application runs on private servers and needs controlled client ingress and outbound access.
patterns.avoid: NAT is outbound connectivity, never a serial hop between the client and application load balancer.
patterns.flow: Client -> load balancer -> private application -> selected data service; application -> NAT -> internet only when egress is needed.
patterns.layout: Align ingress, application and data. Show selected AZs as parallel lanes, with shared services beside them.
service_choices: An internet-facing ALB uses public subnets; private servers receive traffic from the ALB.
Auto Scaling and multiple AZs support resilience when selected; S3 gateway access can avoid NAT for that path.
relationship_checks: Keep request and egress arrows distinct.
Do not infer a public entry point for an internal-only application.
deployment_checks: Public NAT belongs in public subnets; application servers in private subnets.
Identify which subnets and AZs each selected resource actually uses.

patterns.title: Container orchestration and compute choice
patterns.use_when: The selected application needs a container runtime or already has container packaging.
patterns.avoid: Do not choose Kubernetes simply because containers are mentioned or replace an agreed platform.
patterns.flow: Ingress -> container service -> dependencies; image registry -> runtime is a deployment path.
patterns.layout: Place the runtime on the request path and registry in a separate deployment band.
service_choices: ECS provides container orchestration; EKS fits a Kubernetes operating model.
Fargate provides managed compute for supported ECS/EKS workloads; EC2 provides host-level capacity choices.
ECR stores images; it is not a request-processing service.
relationship_checks: Name both orchestration and compute choices without treating them as consecutive processing steps.

patterns.title: Database replatforming and change capture
patterns.use_when: An existing database moves to a selected target with a defined cutover approach.
patterns.avoid: DMS does not copy a separate filesystem/media library; do not put replication on every live application request.
patterns.flow: Source database -> native migration tool or DMS -> target database; application -> target after validated cutover.
patterns.layout: Use a migration lane alongside the steady-state application path, with source outside the target boundary.
service_choices: Compare native backup/restore for an acceptable outage against CDC for tighter cutover needs.
Assess schema conversion for heterogeneous engines; RDS/Aurora are candidate managed targets, not automatic replacements.
relationship_checks: Show source, replication mechanism and target with correct direction.
Keep validation, cutover and rollback responsibilities explicit rather than promising zero downtime.

patterns.title: File and media migration
patterns.use_when: Files or objects must move between supported source and destination storage.
patterns.avoid: Do not substitute database replication for file transfer or assume every DataSync task requires an agent.
patterns.flow: Source storage -> transfer task -> destination storage; verify copied data and record failures.
patterns.layout: Separate bulk transfer from the application's later media-read path.
service_choices: DataSync handles supported storage transfers; evaluate an SDK copy worker for an unsupported or very small transfer.
Determine agent requirements from the source, destination and transfer mode.
relationship_checks: Name both storage endpoints and the copy direction.
Include verification and handling of files modified during transfer.

patterns.title: Persistence chosen by data and access patterns
patterns.use_when: Persistent application state needs a database choice grounded in queries, consistency and existing technology.
patterns.avoid: Do not replace SQL with DynamoDB without checking joins, access patterns and migration scope; a cache is not automatically the system of record.
patterns.flow: Application reads/writes -> selected authoritative store; add a cache or index only for a justified access need.
patterns.layout: Place the primary store next to its owning application, with derived stores on a separate branch.
service_choices: RDS/Aurora fit relational requirements; DynamoDB fits key-value access with an appropriate key design.
Choose specialist graph, document or in-memory stores only when their data model is needed.
relationship_checks: Identify the authoritative store and any derived copies; do not chain unrelated databases.

patterns.title: RDS Multi-AZ availability versus read scaling
patterns.use_when: The design selects an RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with one standby for availability.
patterns.avoid: Do not send read traffic to this standby or apply this topology unmodified to Aurora or RDS Multi-AZ DB clusters.
patterns.flow: Application -> primary database; primary -> synchronous standby in another AZ; failover changes the active target.
patterns.layout: Show primary and standby in parallel AZs with a short replication link, not two serial processing stages.
service_choices: A single-standby Multi-AZ deployment supports failover; read replicas or a suitable cluster support read scaling.
relationship_checks: Label replication separately from application queries.
Do not claim an availability target merely from selecting Multi-AZ.

patterns.title: Durable jobs and human approval
patterns.use_when: A job spans multiple tasks or waits for an approved external decision.
patterns.avoid: An HTTP success response is not proof that an asynchronous job completed; Express does not support callback-wait or .sync patterns.
patterns.flow: Submit -> state machine -> task -> completion/result -> next task; review branch -> authorized callback -> resume or reject.
patterns.layout: Use one orchestration group with short task branches; place the reviewer beside its decision point.
service_choices: Step Functions Standard supports eligible job-wait and task-token integrations; verify support for the selected service.
Choose an explicit completion mechanism, timeout and failure path.
relationship_checks: Protect and correlate callback tokens; show how approval returns to the waiting job.
Do not draw orchestration control as if it carried the entire document payload.

patterns.title: Queues, notifications and event routing
patterns.use_when: Independent components exchange work, notifications or routed events.
patterns.avoid: Do not add SQS, SNS and EventBridge together without distinct roles; an event bus is not a job-state database.
patterns.flow: Producer -> selected queue/topic/bus -> intended consumers; processing failures follow an explicit recovery path.
patterns.layout: Show actual fan-out branches and separate operational notifications from the core transaction.
service_choices: SQS buffers work for consumers; SNS distributes notifications to subscribers; EventBridge matches events to targets.
Select ordering and duplicate-handling behaviour deliberately; do not promise exactly-once business effects.
relationship_checks: A consumer must process queued work; a queue alone cannot perform a task.
Only add subscriptions and routes required by the selected workflow.

patterns.title: Governed data producers and consumers
patterns.use_when: Multiple producers publish datasets for controlled analytical consumption.
patterns.avoid: Do not turn a simple object archive into a multi-account lake or copy every analytical service.
patterns.flow: Producers -> stored datasets; producers publish metadata -> central catalog; authorized consumers discover and query datasets.
patterns.layout: Separate production, catalog/governance and consumption; distinguish metadata arrows from data reads.
service_choices: S3 holds datasets; Glue Data Catalog describes them; Lake Formation manages selected sharing permissions.
Choose query/processing services for actual consumers and preserve existing account ownership.
relationship_checks: A catalog entry is metadata, not the data payload.
Cross-account access needs an explicit sharing and permission design.

patterns.title: Streaming ingestion and independent consumers
patterns.use_when: A continuous stream of records needs real-time consumption and retention for replay.
patterns.avoid: Do not add a streaming platform for an occasional file upload; Kinesis does not transform records by itself.
patterns.flow: Producers -> Kinesis Data Streams -> consumers -> selected result stores; delivery streams may archive data.
patterns.layout: Use producer, stream and consumer columns; parallel consumers are branches, not sequential processors.
service_choices: Kinesis Data Streams retains records for consumers; choose consumer compute separately.
Data Firehose is a delivery option when the workload needs delivery to supported destinations.
relationship_checks: State partitioning, retention and replay assumptions; do not invent throughput or shard counts.

patterns.title: Tenant-aware shared and dedicated resources
patterns.use_when: Multiple tenants share one product with explicit isolation requirements.
patterns.avoid: Do not equate shared hosting with permission to read other tenants' data, or require one account per tenant without justification.
patterns.flow: Tenant identity -> authorized application -> tenant-scoped resources; shared onboarding and operations manage tenants.
patterns.layout: Separate shared control functions from tenant data paths; label actual isolation boundaries.
service_choices: Silo dedicates resources; pool shares them; bridge combines approaches by tier.
Select tenancy based on isolation, cost and operational needs before choosing services.
relationship_checks: Carry tenant context to each data access.
Show dedicated and shared tiers accurately rather than drawing a box as a security guarantee.

patterns.title: Private access to regional storage services
patterns.use_when: VPC resources need access to S3 or DynamoDB through selected private routing.
patterns.avoid: Do not draw S3/DynamoDB inside a subnet or call a gateway endpoint a PrivateLink interface endpoint.
patterns.flow: Workload -> associated route table's gateway endpoint -> regional S3/DynamoDB service.
patterns.layout: Keep the endpoint at the VPC boundary and the managed service in regional space.
service_choices: Gateway endpoints support S3 and DynamoDB without a NAT or internet gateway for that path.
Compare interface endpoints where gateway-endpoint routing does not fit the required access.
relationship_checks: Check route-table association and endpoint/resource permissions.
A gateway endpoint is not universal access to every AWS service.

patterns.title: Application users and federated identity
patterns.use_when: Named users need authenticated sessions or federation with an existing identity provider.
patterns.avoid: IAM execution roles do not replace end-user sign-in; do not replace an existing IdP without scope approval.
patterns.flow: User -> identity provider -> tokens; application validates authorized API requests and applies resource-level permissions.
patterns.layout: Put identity next to ingress, with a token relationship rather than routing all business data through it.
service_choices: Cognito user pools support app sign-in and OIDC/SAML federation.
Identity pools provide AWS credentials where direct AWS resource access is required; they are a separate choice.
relationship_checks: Specify who validates tokens and where case/tenant permissions are enforced.
Closed reviewer access does not imply public self-registration.

patterns.title: Security ownership and shared controls
patterns.use_when: Security controls span workloads or accounts and ownership must be explicit.
patterns.avoid: The security reference is a menu of options, not a requirement to deploy every security product for a POC.
patterns.flow: Workload activity -> selected monitoring/audit collection -> responsible security or operations account; control configuration is a separate path.
patterns.layout: Keep the application story central; group shared controls by purpose and real account ownership.
service_choices: Evaluate identity, encryption, secrets, audit and monitoring against threat exposure and responsibilities.
Separate management, security tooling, log archive and workload roles only where the selected environment requires them.
relationship_checks: Do not draw decorative arrows from every control to every workload node.
Functional security groups are not automatically VPCs or subnets.

patterns.title: Recovery selected by business objectives
patterns.use_when: Recovery objectives, scope and cost justify a recovery design.
patterns.avoid: Do not equate Multi-AZ availability with recovery from a regional disaster or invent an active-active deployment.
patterns.flow: Primary state -> selected backup/replication target; recovery procedure -> restored or promoted service -> redirected clients.
patterns.layout: Separate primary and recovery locations; distinguish replication from failover traffic.
service_choices: Compare backup/restore, pilot light, warm standby and active-active against RPO, RTO and cost.
Choose supported backup/replication mechanisms for the actual services and test recovery.
relationship_checks: Show what is copied and what must be provisioned during recovery.
Mark unconfirmed recovery objectives as open decisions.

patterns.title: Approval-gated operational remediation
patterns.use_when: Operational changes require an identified approver before execution.
patterns.avoid: Do not let model output bypass the approval gate or assume every employee Windows device is enrolled in Systems Manager.
patterns.flow: Incident/diagnosis -> proposed action -> approve or deny -> permitted execution -> validation -> ticket update/escalation.
patterns.layout: Place approval before the action; branch denial/escalation away from execution.
service_choices: Systems Manager Automation offers approval-paused runbooks where the target and permissions fit.
An existing endpoint-management tool may execute approved actions; retain the agreed ticketing system.
relationship_checks: Identify approvers and notification delivery; confirm target enrollment and connectivity separately.
AWS runbook approval is a conditional implementation, not proof of Freshdesk or WMI integration.

patterns.title: Cost tracking and budget notifications
patterns.use_when: The project requires visibility into spend or cost/usage threshold notifications.
patterns.avoid: Budget notifications are delayed and are not a guaranteed hard spending cap.
patterns.flow: Billing/usage data -> AWS Budgets -> responsible email/SNS recipient; approved budget actions are separate controls.
patterns.layout: Place budget controls in an operations band, outside the application request path.
service_choices: AWS Budgets tracks actual/forecasted cost and usage; scope thresholds to the agreed account/project.
Choose optional actions explicitly; do not assume a notification stops all resources.
relationship_checks: Keep cost alerts distinct from CloudWatch workload alarms.
Do not invent threshold amounts or current prices from this reference.

patterns.title: Connectivity between customer networks and AWS
patterns.use_when: AWS workloads must communicate with private customer networks.
patterns.avoid: Do not assume a provisioned dedicated circuit, zero latency or automatic end-to-end redundancy.
patterns.flow: Customer network -> selected VPN/dedicated connectivity -> VPC or routing hub -> private workload.
patterns.layout: Keep customer ownership outside AWS and show the actual network entry point.
service_choices: Site-to-Site VPN uses IPsec over internet connectivity; Direct Connect provides a dedicated connection.
Transit Gateway is useful for selected multi-network routing; it is not needed for every single-VPC POC.
relationship_checks: Check non-overlapping address ranges, routing and required redundancy.
Separate connectivity provisioning dependencies from application implementation.

patterns.title: Queued compute-intensive batch jobs
patterns.use_when: Queued jobs need compute capacity selected for their resource requirements.
patterns.avoid: Do not select Batch just because an upload contains several documents, or treat every long-running job as a Lambda.
patterns.flow: Submitter -> batch queue/scheduler -> selected compute job -> results storage; execution status returns to job tracking.
patterns.layout: Keep scheduling, compute and output distinct; deployment artifacts are supporting dependencies.
service_choices: AWS Batch schedules jobs and provisions supported compute; choose EC2/Fargate/EKS arrangements from workload needs.
Confirm resource and accelerator support instead of copying reference instance sizes.
relationship_checks: Name the execution environment and result destination; a queue alone performs no computation.
